reason: This book was rescreened and entered at the 2026-09-16 close, which was itself the post-FOMC print: the 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, the 12-0 vote and the hawkish dot plot (16 of 18 officials penciling one more hike this year) were all in the tape when these fills happened. So the macro fact that would justify a rescreen has not changed since entry; I have only three sessions of noise. The leg is -0.84% of NAV, decomposing into -0.34% from the 54.7% long basket and -0.51% from the 40.3% SPY short (SPY +1.26% against me on a tech-led Thursday bounce). For a beta-matched, nine-sector, thirteen-name residual book that is comfortably inside one sigma over three days; treating it as evidence would be confusing a weekly mark with a signal. Second, and more concretely, I would be rescreening off 2026-09-18 closes, and 2026-09-18 was September quadruple witching with roughly $6tn of options exposure expiring plus quarterly index rebalancing. Those closes carry pin and roll distortion in exactly the cross-sectional dimension my screen reads - residual vol and pairwise residual correlation - and a meaningful share of Friday's single-name dispersion typically reverses in the following week. Rebuilding a residual-correlation screen on witching prints is the single worst day of the quarter to do it. Third, the 2026 factor backdrop still argues for the structure as built: equal-weight has beaten cap-weight by about five points year to date and leadership has broadened into financials, industrials and healthcare, so a diversified nine-sector long basket financed by a cap-weighted SPY short is long the factor that has been paying, and the last two sessions' mega-cap tech bounce is the counter-move a dispersion book is supposed to sit through rather than chase. Fourth, the design premise is intact: the offsetting macro loadings were chosen for a rate-up world and we now have an explicit restarting hiking cycle, which is the regime CME and GPN were sized for, and the basket still holds no AI-capex names, so my residual is stock selection rather than a bet on the AI complex. Fifth, the one leg whose thesis the hiking cycle genuinely degrades is CHTR: 4.4x net debt/EBITDA, 2.4x interest cover, a $90bn+ stack being refinanced at 7%+ coupons after the Liberty Broadband and Cox closes, and it is already my worst mark at -5.06%. But it is 3.2% of the book with a -20% stop, so the entire remaining downside I am underwriting there is about 48bps of NAV, and the only way this format lets me remove it is to replace all fourteen legs - repricing the other twelve longs and the SPY short at Monday's close, resetting every stop reference away from fills I understand, and paying spread and SEC/TAF across the whole $950 of gross. Paying a full-book turn to excise one contained 3.2% position is a bad trade. Finally, turnover discipline: this is leg 8 in nine weeks. A dispersion book earns from residual convergence that needs weeks to express, and rescreening every Monday guarantees I pay the costs of the strategy while never holding a position long enough to collect its payoff. The screen is three days old, it was built on the right information, and the correct action is to let it work.
